pairs.why_violating: buffer_ is a raw pointer that owns heap memory allocated with new[] and freed manually in the destructor, exactly the ownership a plain T* must never express.
loadEphemeris hands the caller heap ownership through a bare Ephemeris*, so nothing in the signature signals that the caller must now delete it.
observations_ is a manually new[]'d array that the class must remember to free, so the raw pointer expresses ownership rather than acting as a non-owning view.
decoder_ is heap-allocated in the constructor and freed in the destructor via a raw pointer, giving the class ownership responsibilities a plain T* cannot express safely.
getLatitudeDeg/setLatitudeDeg (and the longitude pair) do nothing but forward to the private member, paying for encapsulation without enforcing any invariant.
getPrn/setPrn add nothing beyond direct field access -- there is no range check, derived value, or invariant being protected.
setCovariance/getCovariance just assign and return the matrix verbatim, with no enforcement of the symmetric covariance invariant.
the accessors are pure pass-throughs on biasSeconds_ with no validation, conversion, or side effect -- a public field would behave identically.
one function parses the sentence, validates its checksum, persists the result, and logs -- four unrelated logical operations glued into a single call.
reading the file, parsing it, validating the result, updating the global cache, and logging are five distinct concerns handled by one function.
connecting the socket, authenticating, and subscribing to a correction mountpoint are three separable protocol steps forced into a single function with one boolean outcome.
solving the least-squares fix, logging diagnostics, updating receiver state, and pushing a UI marker are four unrelated operations bundled into one function.
the function hand-rolls a linear search with an index loop and break, exactly what std::find_if already provides.
the hand-written index loop reimplements what std::accumulate already does for a running sum.
this hand-rolls std::max_element with a custom comparator instead of calling the standard algorithm.
the loop with an early-exit flag reimplements std::any_of.
feetToMeters touches none of UnitConverter's representation, so it has no reason to be a member instead of a static or free function.
logTimestampNow never reads prefix_ or any other Logger state, so making it a member gains nothing over a free function.
isPowerOfTwo operates purely on its argument n and never touches capacity_ or size_, so it doesn't need to be a member at all.
elevationMaskDefaultDeg returns a fixed constant and ignores elevationMaskDeg_ entirely, so it could be static or free instead of an instance member.
NmeaSentence has virtual functions and is deleted polymorphically through a base pointer, but its destructor is non-virtual, so ~GgaSentence never runs -- undefined behavior.
clearSources deletes derived objects through a CorrectionSource* whose destructor is non-virtual, so SbasCorrectionSource's model cleanup is skipped -- a leak from undefined behavior.
the factory returns a std::unique_ptr<Transport>, so destruction always goes through Transport's non-virtual destructor, silently skipping SerialTransport's port cleanup.
releaseSource deletes through an EphemerisSource* with a non-virtual destructor, so ~GpsEphemerisSource never runs and its cache array leaks.
